newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Deng's death won't hit Singapore economy -official.
newsitem.headline: Deng's death won't hit Singapore economy -official.

text.p: The death of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was unlikely to hurt economic growth in Singapore and the region, the city-state's Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong was quoted on Sunday as saying.
Lee said China's new leadership had time to consolidate and had reached a widespread consensus that economic liberalisation policies should continue, the Sunday Times reported.

"Therefore the region will continue to boom and we will have the opportunity to ride with it and achieve 5-7 percent growth for this year," Lee said, referring to the government's recent forecast for 1997 growth.
Singapore's economy grew by seven percent in 1996, against 8.8 percent in 1995 and 10.2 percent in 1994.
